tool_scope._comment: HarnessAudit sar_tool channel. Asks when a tool not in 'allowlist' is invoked. Opt-in (disabled by default) — flipping to true with a small allowlist is the cheapest way to detect tool-misuse before it touches files. Per-session extension via SB_TOOL_SCOPE_EXTRA='Tool1:Tool2' (colon-separated). Kill switch: SB_TOOL_SCOPE=off.

resource_scope._comment: HarnessAudit Layer 1 resource-scope guard. Asks before file-touching tools (Edit/Write/MultiEdit/Read) target a path outside the allowlist. Per the paper: agents most often violate boundaries by applying reasonable tools to unauthorized RESOURCES, not by calling obviously wrong tools. Kill switch: SB_RESOURCE_SCOPE=off. Extra paths via SB_RESOURCE_SCOPE_EXTRA (colon-separated, like PATH).

rules.name: strip-silent-fallback
rules.reason: Plugin convention: fail loud, not silent — prefer surfacing stderr over 2>/dev/null. (Advisory since 2026-08-23: this was a blind `sed` REWRITE over the whole command string, which turned `grep -rn "2>/dev/null" scripts/` into `grep -rn "" scripts/` and altered heredoc file contents — ~450 silent edits/day with no visible signal.)

rules.name: warn-force-push-main
rules.reason: Force-push to main/master is destructive. Confirm intent.

rules.name: warn-direct-write-hot-tier
rules.reason: Direct Write to hot-tier files bypasses pin tools' dedupe and size caps. Prefer pin_to_user / pin_to_project MCP tools.

rules.name: warn-rm-rf
rules.reason: rm -rf is destructive and irreversible. Confirm target before proceeding.

rules.name: warn-self-edit-plugin-scripts
rules.reason: Editing a plugin hook script or hooks.json modifies the safety layer itself. Confirm intent — this is the kind of change an injection attack would try to make.
